title: kv memory sieve and chronological eviction proxy to reduce fragmentation and spill spikes
author: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight 'memory sieve' allocator and a Chronological Eviction Proxy for the KV cache to reduce micro-fragmentation and smooth spillover spikes to disk; includes allocator tiering for small vs large page regions, a hinting API for async compaction, integration hooks for the batching/scheduler layer to avoid eviction during critical tail-latency windows, and metrics/bench harness updates. Motivation: customers running long-lived chat workloads saw periodic spill spikes under skewed token distributions that degraded P95 latency and caused disk I/O storms. The change targets three pain points: 1) tiny allocation fragmentation caused by variable-sized KV segments, 2) synchronous eviction cascades that coincide with heavy batching windows, and 3) lack of compaction feedback into the runtime scheduler. This PR implements a sieve allocator that routes sub-page allocations into shared slab pools, a non-blocking compaction hint path that schedules background merges, and a Chronological Eviction Proxy that orders candidates by last-use chronology with tenant-aware admission to avoid mass eviction in a single pass. Includes microbench results, rollout plan, and safer default configs for Dedicated clusters.
